 Advertisement Updated: 4:50 PM EDT Oct 29, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Chloe McCoy Digital Content Producer Former Spartanburg County music teacher sentenced in child exploitation case
 Updated: 4:50 PM EDT Oct 29, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Chloe McCoy Digital Content Producer SPARTANBURG, S.C. — A former Spartanburg County music teacher has been sentenced after pleading guilty in a child sexual exploitation case , according to the South Carolina Attorney General's Office. 
 Spartanburg Police John Foster Jr. 78-year-old John Foster Jr. recently pleaded guilty to three charges. He received a 10-year sentence, with all but 90 days suspended. 
 Advertisement Police: Man charged with DUI after Simpsonville crash causes power outage for hundreds of residents Prosecutors said Foster will serve those 90 days on weekends while spending weekdays on home detention. During the home detention, he will only be allowed to leave for medical appointments and church.
 Officials also said Foster will be placed on the sex offender registry and under GPS monitoring.
 SCHP: Driver killed in four-vehicle crash in Spartanburg County There is also a permanent restraining order in place to ensure Foster will have no contact with the victim for the remainder of his life, according to prosecutors. 
 After his first arrest, police said Foster was a music instructor at Roper Music on East Main Street in Spartanburg.
 Spartanburg deputies seek help identifying person in Target theft investigation Roper Music sent a statement to WYFF News 4 and said the following:
 "Roper Music rented an instruction room to Randy Foster to teach guitar lessons to his students. Randy was not an employee of Roper Music; he had a lease agreement to rent space for lessons. As soon as we were notified that Randy had been arrested, we terminated his lease immediately. The case is still in the judicial system, and we don't have any updates to share. This is an unfortunate situation, and we rely on the justice system to reveal the truth."
